subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Has No Common Sense
description: A micro-lesson that makes AI Has No Common Sense usable.

hook.text: Ask AI: 'Can a fish climb a tree?' It might say yes — if the training data was ambiguous.

buildup.text: Humans absorb common sense from living in the world. AI only reads about it.

discovery.text: Models lack grounded experience — they've never held an object or felt gravity.

twist.text: A model can write a recipe for lemonade but doesn't know lemons are sour.

climax.text: Researchers have spent decades trying to encode common sense. No one has cracked it yet.

quiz.question: Why does AI lack common sense?
options: It learns from text, not from physical experience
It's too slow to process real-world data
It's intentionally designed to avoid assumptions

details.summary: AI lacks the vast background knowledge humans acquire through everyday experience. It can process information far faster than humans but fails at basic reasoning about physical, social, and temporal common sense.
details.whyItMatters: Common sense failures make AI unreliable in real-world situations. A self-driving car or medical AI that lacks basic reasoning about the world can make dangerous mistakes.
takeaways: AI cannot reason about the physical world like humans can
Social and temporal common sense are especially absent
This gap limits AI reliability in open-ended real-world tasks

faq.question: Can large language models use common sense?
faq.answer: LLMs approximate common sense in many text-based scenarios because they have read descriptions of common sense reasoning. But they fail on novel physical scenarios and unusual edge cases that require genuine understanding.

faq.question: Why is common sense so hard to program?
faq.answer: Common sense encompasses billions of implicit facts about how the world works. Humans learn it through years of embodied experience. Encoding all this knowledge explicitly in a system has proven intractable.
